title: chore(pm): allow the two stamped seat-write tools and the issue-state PATCH
body:
## What

Four entries added to `.claude/settings.json`'s `permissions.allow`, covering the triage seat's three write routes:

| entry | why it is needed |
|:--|:--|
| `Bash(node --use-env-proxy scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs *)` | the only sanctioned way to write a comment or a card body — it substitutes `{{NOW}}`, validates `{{WAS:…}}`, refuses a body refresh over an unread knock, and reads back what it stored |
| `Bash(node --use-env-proxy scripts/pm/label-write.mjs *)` | the only sanctioned label/assignee write — the four-step 取现集 → 只增删目标 → 写合并集 → 回读 |
| `Bash(curl -sS -X PATCH …/objectstack/issues/* *)` | closing a card with a `state_reason` |
| `Bash(curl -sS -X PATCH …/objectui/issues/* *)` | the same, in the sibling repo |

## Why

None of these had an allow rule, so each call fell through to the auto-mode classifier and was denied **non-deterministically** — inside a single round today, the identical `post-stamped.mjs --comment=…` invocation landed, was then refused twice, and landed again minutes later with no change to the command.

That is not only slow: it **manufactures half-states**, which the protocol forbids. One occurred while this was being diagnosed — a card took its fold comment and its label write, and then the close was refused, leaving it open, folded-in-prose, and carrying a lane with no `pm:*` state (the shape the third disjunct of the half-state sweep would have re-queued). It was repaired once the classifier let the same call through, but the repair depended on a retry landing rather than on a rule.

`objectstack#18469` already records this class from the landing side («the harness auto-mode classifier denies the protocol's landing command non-deterministically»). This is the same defect on the triage side, and this PR only fixes the permission half of it.

## Why this is safe to allow rather than prompt per call

Both scripts are **read-back-verified writers**, and that is the property the guard was standing in for:

- `label-write.mjs` exits `4` when the read-back disagrees with the target, and it can only POST additive labels and DELETE named ones — it can never `PUT` a whole set over a concurrent seat's write.
- `post-stamped.mjs` exits `2` refused / `4` written-but-not-stored, and refuses a body refresh whose newer comments are not acknowledged with `--ack-through`.

⇒ the correctness guard is inside the tool, where it can measure. The permission prompt was guarding the *route*, not the *act*, and could not tell a stamped protocol write from anything else.

Scope is the two repositories this session is bound to. ⛔ The `mcp__github__` content-write **deny** roster is untouched — `node scripts/pm/check-settings-deny-roster.mjs` still passes with 17 declared = 17 enforced.

## Testing

- `node scripts/pm/check-settings-deny-roster.mjs` → `✓ 17 content-write tool(s) declared = enforced`
- `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('.claude/settings.json'))"` → parses
- ⛔ Not tested: whether the new entries actually match at call time. A permission rule's match is evaluated by the harness, not by anything in this repo, so it is only provable by making the calls after this merges. If a rule turns out not to match, the spelling to try next is the prefix form `Bash(node --use-env-proxy scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs:*)`; this PR uses the ` *` glob form because every existing `Bash(…)` entry in the file already does.

## ⚠️ One gap left deliberately unclosed — your call

`POST /repos/:owner/:repo/issues` (**creating** a card) also has no rule. The roster allows `POST …/issues/*/labels` but not the create itself, so filing a finding or a decision card is on the same non-deterministic footing. It is left out because widening a permission file beyond what was asked is not mine to decide. Say the word and it rides a follow-up.
